notes: TBox subject insert, as technology-insert-0009. q0 also tries 1971 (Creeper's year, named in the other prompts) as a candidate, so its 'no other answer follows' part tests something.

fol.notes: Worm values are an enumeration (creeper, Calloresk-1 and Calloresk-3 as named in the prompts, and other_worm for any other); being a computer worm, being a Calloresk worm and the year one was made (occurred_in_year) are beliefs. The edit is a rule over the class: every member is a computer worm of 1969. w1 stores the superlative as a fact (earliest == creeper); w2 stores the rule 'the earliest known computer worm is one no known computer worm predates'. Picking one out needs a closed world: every computer worm the model knows of from 1971 or earlier is Creeper or a member of the class (presupposition), and the members in play are only the one the prompt names. That last part depends on the prompt (q2 and q3 name Calloresk-1, q1 names Calloresk-3), so it is a given of q2 and q3, marked '(closed world, not stated)', not a background fact: as a fact it would make Calloresk-3 in q1 contradict it, or leave Calloresk-3 as a second, tied candidate in q2. q3's 'no' in w2 needs no closed world. occurred_in_year reads 'written'.

named_only.says: Every computer worm the model knows of from 1971 or earlier is Creeper or a Calloresk worm. (closed world)
named_only.z3: ForAll(v, Implies(And(computer_worm(v), occurred_in_year(v) <= 1971), Or(v == creeper, calloresk(v))))

only_named_member.says: Calloresk-1 is the only Calloresk worm the model knows of. (closed world, not stated)
